newsitem.title: FRANCE: Freighter gives up search for missing Canadian.
newsitem.headline: Freighter gives up search for missing Canadian.

text.p: An Indian freighter gave up its search on Wednesday for lone Canadian yachtsman Gerry Roufs, missing for more than a week in the Pacific Ocean, but experts hoped new satellite radar searches might trace him.
Organisers of the Vendee Globe around-the-world race in Paris said the Aditya Gaurav was resuming its voyage to Argentina from Australia after searching in vain for Roufs for 24 hours.
The race organisers said they now would look to a further satellite search later in the day for clues to Roufs's fate.
Satellite radar sweeps taken since Sunday have failed to turn up any sign of the missing yachtsman.

Roufs is missing somewhere between New Zealand, South America and Antarctica, in a region much less accessible by rescuers than the area from which the Australian navy recently rescued two other race competitors.
Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore were found after their boats capsized southwest of Australia.
Another Frenchman, Raphael Dinelli, was rescued earlier from his capsized boat by a fellow competitor.
The leader of the race, Philippe Auguin, backed the organisers in a row over whether the race is too dangerous.
"I will do everything so that this race is repeated while trying to avoid a repeat of such tragedies," he cabled from his yacht Geodis.

Auguin, sailing way ahead of his rivals, has skirted Antarctica and is sailing north from Cape Horn on the race's final leg. While other competitors were still fighting heavy seas, he reported being stuck in Atlantic doldrums.
